title: Mia · Help without taking over
orientation: Twelve linked moments about help, choice and being heard. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each next scene is a new moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: Help from Alex brings gratitude and a lost chance to answer.
scenes.prompt: Reflect both meanings of the help.
scenes.text: [Half-smiles] Alex means well. I’m grateful right up until he starts answering for me.
scenes.suggestion: You welcome his care, and lose something important when your own answer gets replaced.

scenes.bridge: Mia asks how exploration could help with mixed feelings.
scenes.prompt: Explain listening to both wishes without judging one away.
scenes.text: [Unsure] Part of me wants help. Part of me hates being helped. How does talking untangle that?
scenes.suggestion: We could hear what each part wants in one real moment, rather than decide that one is wrong.

scenes.bridge: Another helpful act leaves a choice missing.
scenes.prompt: Validate appreciation alongside the missing choice.
scenes.text: [Guilty] Alex did the shopping. I thanked him, but I missed choosing things myself.
scenes.suggestion: You can appreciate the effort and miss a choice that mattered. Those feelings don’t cancel each other.

scenes.bridge: Mia distinguishes wanting the offer from how it arrived.
scenes.prompt: Ask about the difficult part of the offer.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I didn’t want the offer to stop. Just... something about how it came.
scenes.suggestion: What about the way he offered felt difficult?

scenes.bridge: A wish for a say is present, followed by self-judgment.
scenes.prompt: Make space for that wish before judging its tone.
scenes.text: [Angry, hesitant] I want my say. Then I hear myself sounding ungrateful.
scenes.suggestion: Could we give the wish for a say a moment, before judging its tone?

scenes.bridge: In another moment, Mia can describe the tasks but not her quiet.
scenes.prompt: Offer one tentative meaning and leave room for correction.
scenes.text: [Brisk] I can list exactly what Alex did. I can’t explain why I went quiet.
scenes.suggestion: Perhaps the help was useful, while not being asked left you feeling less included?

scenes.bridge: She describes being behind the helpful action.
scenes.prompt: Bring her description closer without enlarging it.
scenes.text: [Distant] Alex does the helpful thing. I’m somewhere behind it, getting cross.
scenes.suggestion: Is it like the task moves forward while your chance to choose gets left behind?

scenes.bridge: A wish for a say shifts toward excusing Alex.
scenes.prompt: Keep his care in view while inviting a return to her experience.
scenes.text: [Angry, then excuses] I wanted a say. But Alex had a busy day, so never mind.
scenes.suggestion: His day can matter too. Would you like us to return to what having a say meant there?

scenes.bridge: A later moment is angry and tearful, with Mia still present.
scenes.prompt: Listen for what she wants heard without speeding up.
scenes.text: [Angry, voice shaking] I want you to hear this. I’m worried you’ll hear only the anger.
scenes.suggestion: I’m listening for what you want heard, not just the anger. We can take it slowly.

scenes.bridge: Another moment shows the cost of the offers stopping altogether.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the choice she wanted and the help she misses.
scenes.text: [Angry, then guilty] I wanted Alex to leave the plants alone. Now he won’t offer at all.
scenes.suggestion: You wanted a choice about that help, and now miss having the offer.

scenes.bridge: Mia finds a distinction within the help she wants.
scenes.prompt: Explore what her new words make clearer.
scenes.text: [Relieved] “Ask, then wait” is what I meant. I don’t mean never help me.
scenes.suggestion: What do those words make clearer about the help you want?

scenes.bridge: Time is nearly over; using the words remains her choice.
scenes.prompt: End without turning the request into homework.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I found words for Alex, but I don’t know if I want to use them tonight.
scenes.suggestion: You don’t need to use them tonight. Shall we note them and check what fits your evening instead?
